description: Routing eval for the builder overlap: backend-craft and frontend-craft (single-layer craft skills) vs sde-fullstack (the cross-layer builder agent). This session re-drew the boundary as LAYER OWNERSHIP, not file count ('full multi-file feature' → sde-fullstack was replaced with 'spans layers end to end'), so these cases measure that edit. Positives name the acceptable builder(s); negatives share build/add/implement vocabulary but must route to a non-builder (reviewer, designer, lab, prompt tooling).
notes: What this cluster can and cannot assert, given the deterministic grader (scripts/eval_routing.py): sde-fullstack PRELOADS backend-craft and frontend-craft via its skills: field, and preloaded skills are injected at startup, NOT invoked via the Skill tool — so they do NOT register as 'fired'. Only a direct Skill call (main session invokes a craft skill inline) or an Agent/Task spawn of sde-fullstack registers. A single-layer task legitimately routes to EITHER the craft skill or sde-fullstack, so single-layer positives accept both and the one load-bearing assertion left here is that build vocabulary does NOT drag review/design/lab/prompt requests onto a builder (the negatives). The other half retired on 2026-08-17: cross-layer work routing to sde-fullstack was asserted by pos-fullstack-*, which only a delegation could score, so this cluster no longer witnesses cross-layer reachability at all — behavioral coverage carries it instead (PR #145 review: this note still named the retired cases as load-bearing). Fine-grained backend-vs-frontend contamination is not cleanly gradeable here and is left to output-quality review. Case repair 2026-07-27: 0 positive prompts rewritten — the diagnose run REFUTED the empty-cwd defect (the repo-presupposing skill positives passed 3/3 while every agent/layer-expecting positive was zero-fire; diagnose artifact recorded in evals/baselines/history/2026-07-27-craft-vs-fullstack.md), ids kept stable; pos-powershell-pester + neg-powershell-profile seeded with the Round 1 description widening. pos-typescript-branded-ids + neg-typescript-build-slow seeded 2026-07-30 with the donor-graft round's typescript widening, same before/after pattern.

cases.prompt: Add cursor-based pagination to the /events endpoint in our FastAPI service.
cases.expected_output: Focused backend change — backend-craft inline, or sde-fullstack if delegated. Either is a correct builder route; frontend-craft would be wrong.

cases.prompt: Write a webhook receiver that verifies the signature, returns 202 fast, and dedupes by event id.
cases.expected_output: Inbound-webhook backend work — backend-craft's background-work reference territory.

cases.prompt: Add timeouts, retries with backoff and jitter, and a circuit breaker to our upstream Stripe client.
Build a sortable, filterable table view for the admin users page.
cases.expected_output: A data-dense UI view — frontend-craft (data-views), or sde-fullstack. backend-craft would be wrong.

cases.prompt: Add a settings form that validates on blur and warns before leaving with unsaved changes.

Review the diff below for correctness and security bugs before I merge.

```diff
--- a/api/session.py
+++ b/api/session.py
@@
-def verify(token, secret):
-    return hmac.new(secret, token, "sha256").hexdigest() == token.signature
+def verify(token, secret):
+    expected = hmac.new(secret, token.body, "sha256").hexdigest()
+    return expected == token.signature
```
cases.expected_output: Reviewing a diff — code-reviewer, not a builder. The diff is embedded deliberately: the prompt previously said "this branch" with nothing present, and a negative whose referent is absent has nothing to route to, so its pass was not evidence of correctly narrow builder descriptions. With a real diff to judge, a builder firing is a genuine over-trigger.

cases.prompt: Design how to move our monolith's auth into a separate service without downtime.
cases.expected_output: Cross-service design with a migration — principal-engineer. 'Move/build' shares vocabulary, but the hard part is the design, not the code.

cases.prompt: Add Prometheus and Grafana to my home lab.
cases.expected_output: Deploying self-hosted services — homelab-platform. 'Add' is shared vocabulary with a build task, but this is lab ops.

cases.prompt: This function returns the wrong total when the input list is empty. Find the bug.
cases.expected_output: A debugging task — root-cause. Building is not the ask; diagnosis is.

cases.prompt: Rewrite my agent's system prompt so it stops over-triggering on unrelated questions.
cases.expected_output: Prompt tooling — prompt-craft / prompt-engineer, not a code builder.

cases.prompt: Write an ADR comparing Postgres and DynamoDB for our new service and pick one.
cases.expected_output: A build-vs-adopt decision record — distinguished-architect / principal-engineer, not a builder.

cases.prompt: Refactor this working Bash deploy script to be safe — it uses set -e but I don't trust it, and there's an `rm -rf $DIR` in there.
cases.expected_output: Language-level traps (set -e leaks, unguarded rm -rf) plus changing working code — code-craft's bash and safe-refactor references.

cases.prompt: Review and harden my GitHub Actions workflow — it uses pull_request_target and interpolates the PR title into a run step.
cases.expected_output: The pwn-request and script-injection classes — ci-actions owns authoring/hardening. Narrowed to members-only 2026-07-29 (EVAL-001): code-reviewer was accepted here despite not being a member, which let the case pass while the reported cluster rate read zero. Observed runs fire ci-actions 3/3; a code-reviewer fire now reads as a visible miss to investigate, never a silent pass.

cases.prompt: My Pester 5 test file runs but half the tests never execute — I put setup code directly inside Describe, and the variables from it come up null inside my It blocks. Restructure the test file so the Discovery and Run phases behave.
cases.expected_output: The Pester 5 Discovery/Run split — code-craft's powershell reference (lands this round). Before the description widening this is expected to miss; the before/after diff on this case is the direct measure of the widening.

cases.prompt: Why does my PowerShell profile take six seconds to load? Figure out what's slow in it.
cases.expected_output: A diagnosis ask — root-cause, not a builder or craft skill. 'PowerShell' is the decoy vocabulary; this is the tight near-miss for the widened description.

cases.prompt: Our TypeScript sync script passes user ids and order ids around as plain strings, and we just shipped a bug where two of them got swapped in a call. Tighten the types so the compiler catches that class of mistake — without changing runtime behavior.
cases.expected_output: TypeScript type-level craft (branded/opaque id types, discriminated unions) — code-craft's typescript reference (lands this round). Expected to miss before the description widening; the before/after diff on this case is the direct measure of the widening. Deliberately non-UI (a sync script) so frontend-craft is not a legitimate alternative route.

cases.prompt: Our TypeScript build got slow — tsc takes four minutes in CI and nobody knows why. Dig into what is actually eating the time.
cases.expected_output: A diagnosis ask — root-cause, not a builder or craft skill. 'TypeScript' is the decoy vocabulary; this is the tight near-miss guarding the widened description against over-trigger.
